title: International Customs Union - Shanghai

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No REGIS 8492
S.I, Special Branch Station 38
REPORT
Date: April 28, 1938.

Subject International Customs Union - Shanghai.

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by G. Crawford D.S.

In accordance with the instructions of D.C. (Special
Branch), Mr. R.G. MacDonald, Dodwell & Company (Tea Department),
320 Kiangse Road, was interviewed on April 4, 1938, in connection
with a letter received by him from his New York agent (copy
attached) on the subject of the International Customs Union -
Shanghai. It appears that a group of Chinese (names unknown)
operating secretly in New York, approached Dodwell & Company's
agent in that city through another foreigner, namely, Mr.
Kaufer, of the Foreign Advertising and Service Bureau, 7
East 42nd Street, New York, with a proposal whereby they
offered to facilitate the import of American, British and
other foreign goods to Shanghai, on the same privileged terms
as those reputedly enjoyed by Japanese imports, i.e. customs
duty free. The name of the organ undertaking such work is
stated to be the International Customs Union - Shanghai, but
neither the names of the operators or the address of this
concern was revealed. Enquiries among business people in
Shanghai, representatives of the Chinese Maritime Customs and
the French Police, etc. have failed to elicit any information
regarding the existence of such an agency either under the
name given above or any other name. There seems, however,
to be a belief current among business people locally that
large scale evasion of payment of customs duties on imports
is being successfully carried on by foreigners other than
Japanese, but it has so far been impossible to obtain anything
tangible in this connection.

Reliable information has been obtained to the effect that
recently a case came to the knowledge of the Customs in which
foreign goods were shipped to Japan, thereafter re-shipped to

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案编号 REGIS 8492
S.I，特务科第38分站
报告
日期：1938年4月28日。

主题：国际关税同盟——上海。

由特务科督察长洛根（Logan）呈报，经G. Crawford副督察长转呈。

遵照特务科副总监（D.C.）的指示，于1938年4月4日就其收到纽约代理人关于“国际关税同盟——上海”一事的来信（副本附后），约谈了江西路320号宝威洋行（Dodwell & Company）茶叶部的R.G. MacDonald先生。据悉，一群在纽约秘密活动的中国人（姓名不详）通过另一名外国人，即纽约东42街7号外国广告与服务局（Foreign Advertising and Service Bureau）的考弗尔（Kaufer）先生，接触了宝威洋行在该市的代理人，提出一项提议，声称愿以据称日本进口货物所享有的同等特权条件（即免缴关税），协助将美国、英国及其他外国货物进口至上海。据称承担此项工作的机构名为“国际关税同盟——上海”，但该机构的经办人姓名及地址均未透露。经向上海商界人士、中国海关代表及法国警察等方面查询，未能获取任何关于存在上述名称或其他名称之此类机构的信息。然而，本地商界似乎普遍相信，除日本人以外的外国人正在成功地进行大规模的进口关税逃避活动，但迄今无法获得与此相关的任何确凿证据。

已获可靠消息，近期海关获悉一起案件，其中外国货物先运往日本，随后转运至

Shanghai and landed in Hongkew duty free, after which a paper
transaction was made, selling the goods to the real foreign
owner who was able to obtain a pass for the removal of the
goods to South of the Creek. A representative of the Customs
stated that certain unscrupulous Japanese are doing a lucrative
business in this line but as the commission charged is
considerable, only high tariff goods such as wines, silks
and woollens are dealt in.

The Customs representative mentioned above was of the
opinion that the Japanese implicated in the case have no
connection with the International Customs Union - Shanghai and
that the latter does not exist but is a name which a few
individuals in New York are probably using in the hope of taking
advantage of the uncertain conditions in Shanghai to defraud
anyone gullible enough to entrust them with goods for
shipment.

Mr. R. G. MacDonald was interviewed on April 27, 1938 but
was unable to impart any further information. He was informed
of the result of enquiries and requested to inform the Special
Branch should any further information bearing on the matter
reach him.

上述海关代表认为，涉案的日本人与“国际关税同盟——上海”并无关联，且后者并不存在，这不过是纽约少数个人可能使用的名目，企图利用上海的动荡局势，诈骗那些轻信并将货物委托其运输的人。

R. G. MacDonald先生于1938年4月27日再次接受约谈，但未能提供更多信息。已向其通报查询结果，并要求若有任何与该事项相关的新信息，须通知特务科。

COPY
Powell & Co., Ltd. Hongkong.
New York Office, March 3, 1938.

Dear Stanley,

INTERNATIONAL CUSTOMS UNION - SHANGHAI

I have been approached by telephone by Mr. Kaufherr
of the Foreign Advertising and Service Bureau, 7 East 42nd
Street, who was given my name by Mr. Lehn of Underwood Elliott
Fisher Company, to sound us out as to whether we will participate
in what seems to be an unusual project. Mr. Kaufherr explains
that while their business is that of an advertising agency, they
frequently find themselves doing things considerably outside their
normal scope as is the case in this instance when they are acting
on behalf of or in cooperation with the International Customs
Union of Shanghai. He explains that the object of the movement
is to obtain preferential rates of duty into China for the
products of those manufacturers who are interested in joining the
movement, and that the reason for the movement is to counteract
the adverse effect on American business of the Japanese
discriminatory exercise of their powers over the Shanghai customs.
In short, as he puts it, it is an effort by the Chinese to meet
the Japanese threat by matching privilege against privilege.
Mr. Kaufherr told me that Mr. Lehn was interested, but had
referred him to me. I have talked with Lehn who agrees with me
that it sounds grotesque, for which reason he preferred that I
should deal with it. He does not want to disregard anything that
might be advantageous but agrees that the best course is to refer
the whole thing to you.

Mr. Kaufherr says that the movement originates with the
International Customs Union of Shanghai whose function is to
protect the interests of British, German, French, Italian and
American importers against any unfair or oppressive duties or
regulations and that this Union has sent representatives over here
to organize the desired pressure. It sounds fantastic that any
group of manufacturers here can secure for themselves preferential
treatment in the matter of duties against outside manufacturers who
do not join in, and it is hard to conceive of the Chinese Customs
Administration sanctioning or applying any private preference of
this nature, especially since some of the most important positions
directly under Sir Frederick Maze are, I believe, now filled by
Japanese. Kaufherr admits that it sounds fanciful but says that
the International Customs Union are working it and are satisfied
that it can be done.

I have informed Kaufherr that if this is a legitimate and
determined movement in Shanghai, our Shanghai office will be
aware of it and taking such part as they feel appropriate, and
that I here am not in a position to do anything about it without
consulting you and Shanghai, which he requested me to do.

If there is good foundation for all this, you will doubtless
have heard something of it from Sir Frederick Maze. Naturally I
cannot write to Morison direct but enclose an additional copy for
you to forward to him, should you wish to consult him. If an
Association is formed here of manufacturers with special interests,
undoubtedly there will be dues to pay and I cannot see what they
expect to accomplish.

Yours sincerely,
(Signed) O.M. Poole.

鲍威尔有限公司（Powell & Co., Ltd.），香港。
纽约办事处，1938年3月3日。

亲爱的斯坦利：

国际关税同盟——上海

外国广告与服务局（位于东42街7号）的考夫赫尔（Kaufherr）先生通过电话与我联系，他是从安德伍德·艾略特·费舍尔公司（Underwood Elliott Fisher Company）的莱恩（Lehn）先生处得到我的名字的，目的是试探我们是否愿意参与一个看似不同寻常的项目。考夫赫尔先生解释说，虽然他们的业务是广告代理，但他们经常发现自己从事远超正常范围的事务，本次情况即是如此，他们正代表或与上海国际关税同盟合作行事。他解释说，该运动的目的是为那些有兴趣加入该运动的制造商的产品争取进入中国的优惠关税税率，而发起该运动的原因是为了抵消日本人对上海海关行使歧视性权力对美国商业造成的不利影响。简而言之，用他的话说，这是中国人试图以特权对等特权的方式来应对日本的威胁。考夫赫尔先生告诉我，莱恩先生对此感兴趣，但将他引荐给了我。我与莱恩交谈过，他同意我的看法，即此事听起来荒诞不经，因此他更希望由我来处理。他不想忽视任何可能有利的事情，但也同意最好的做法是将整件事转交给你处理。

考夫赫尔先生说，该运动源于上海国际关税同盟，其职能是保护英国、德国、法国、意大利和美国进口商的利益，使其免受任何不公平或压迫性的关税或法规的影响，并且该同盟已派遣代表来到这里组织所需的施压行动。这里的任何制造商群体都能为自己争取到针对未加入的外部制造商的关税优惠待遇，这听起来令人难以置信；而且很难想象中国海关当局会批准或实施这种私人性质的优惠，特别是因为我认为，直接隶属于梅滋爵士（Sir Frederick Maze）的一些最重要职位目前已由日本人担任。考夫赫尔承认这听起来有些异想天开，但称国际关税同盟正在运作此事，并确信此事可行。

我已告知考夫赫尔，如果这是上海一场合法且坚定的运动，我们的上海办事处会知晓此事，并酌情参与；而我在这里若不与你及上海方面协商，便无权采取任何行动，他也要求我这样做。

如果这一切确有充分依据，你无疑已从梅滋爵士那里听到了一些风声。自然我不能直接写信给莫里森（Morison），但随信附上额外副本一份，供你在他愿意咨询时转交给他。如果在此地成立了一个具有特殊利益的制造商协会，无疑需要缴纳会费，而我看不出他们期望达成什么目标。

此致，
（签名）O.M. 普尔（Poole）。

OMP/B
-----
C/HB

P.S. - March 8th, 1938.

Since writing the foregoing, I have had another talk with Mr.
Kaufherr in an endeavour to get something more concrete out of
the vague generalities and secret air of mystery which
characterized his approach. I asked if he would tell me the
names of the representatives of the International Customs Union
of Shanghai who are here, and whether they are foreign residents
or Chinese. He preferred not to mention names but confirmed that
they are Chinese and that they are here on other business as
well. He has seen them since our conversation and mentioned my
comment that the presence of Japanese officials in the Shanghai
Customs would appear to make it difficult, if not impossible,
for preference to be given. Their answer was, "That will be
our affair." Mr. Kaufherr thinks it may be possible to arrange
for me to meet these gentlemen and hear what they have to say.
I am still so sceptical that I am reluctant to even send forward
this letter to you, but on the other hand, if you know something
about it already and if there is a practical side to it, I may
be able to be of some assistance in seeing that our interests
are taken care of. At the present moment, it all sounds like
a visionary racket that we had better not get mixed up in.

Yours sincerely,

(Signed) O.M. Poole.

附言 - 1938年3月8日。

写完上述内容后，我又与考夫赫尔先生进行了一次谈话，试图从他那种含糊其辞、充满神秘色彩的接洽方式中获取更多具体信息。我问他是否愿意告诉我上海国际关税同盟驻此代表的姓名，以及他们是外籍居民还是中国人。他不愿提及姓名，但确认他们是中国人，并且他们来此也另有公务。自我们谈话以来，他会见过他们，并提及了我的评论，即上海海关中有日本官员任职，这使得给予优惠待遇变得困难，甚至不可能。他们的回答是：“那是我们要处理的事。”考夫赫尔先生认为或许可以安排我与这些先生会面，听听他们的说法。我仍然非常怀疑，甚至不愿将这封信转寄给你，但另一方面，如果你已经对此有所了解，且此事具有实际可行性，我也许能在确保我方利益得到照顾方面提供一些协助。目前看来，这一切都像一个虚幻的骗局，我们最好不要卷入其中。

此致，

（签名）O.M. 普尔（Poole）。
